name: Tags input
purpose: A field the user types free values into, each committed as a removable chip. Use it where the vocabulary is the user's own — payment references, labels, search terms — and no list can be offered. The gated Tags atom is the display half of this: same chip, no field.
$provenance-note: NEW at #203 (wave 3b, lane J) against itinerary row 23 (P2, 'Free-entry token field'). Verified absent first-hand: Tags.reference.html EXISTS and is gated, but it is a display atom — grep for <input / contenteditable in it returns nothing, and its meta declares category 'atom' with variants tag and tag-link only. No tags-input snippet or meta existed under any slug.

props.name: max
props.$status: PROPOSED #203, Dave's eye owed — 8 is the reference's illustrative ceiling, not a ruled product limit.

props.name: commitKeys
props.$note: Comma is included because reference lists are habitually comma-separated; blur also commits a pending value rather than discarding it.

props.name: state
props.$note: Same state channel as Input-fields/Textarea — inherited.

props.name: backspaceBehaviour
props.$status: PROPOSED #203, Dave's eye owed. The first Backspace on an empty field ARMS the last chip (an inset outline, announced politely); a second removes it. Immediate removal loses data silently for fast typists, but two keystrokes is more work for everyone.

variants.name: with tags
variants.use: The working state — chips wrap inside the field and the counter reports how many remain.

variants.name: empty
variants.use: A plain one-row field, so it never looks broken before use; the help text states how a value is committed.

tokens.field-border: form/border/default; focus-within form/border/active + a 4px inset bottom stroke; disabled form/border/disabled; refusal a 4px inset rag/error stroke (dark: full rag/error border)
tokens.chip: INHERITED FROM TAGS — 1px form/border/default on transparent, border-radius/control, label text/default, dismiss glyph icon/default. No new chip tokens.
tokens.chip-armed: a 1px inset rule in form/border/active on the chip Backspace is about to take — an outline change, never colour alone
tokens.counter: text/default at .t-cm-legal; the approaching-limit signal is the WORDING, not a weight or a colour
tokens.hit-area: target/min (44px) on the field row. Chip dismiss 24px — the gated Tags value, inherited unchanged.

accessibility.roles: A plain text input — deliberately NOT role=combobox, because there is no list to expand and claiming one would be a lie to AT. Each chip's dismiss is a real button with a purposeful accessible name ('Remove INV-4471').
accessibility.keyboard: Enter or comma commits; blur commits a pending value; Backspace on an empty field arms the last chip and a second Backspace removes it; each dismiss button is tabbable.
accessibility.announcements: A polite live region announces every add, every removal, the armed chip, and each refusal — the chip list changes outside the caret's reading position, so silence would be a data loss the user cannot perceive.
accessibility.states: Refusals set aria-invalid + aria-describedby on the input and render a message that pairs a symbol with words and stays ink. Duplicates and the limit are refused explicitly, never silently dropped.
accessibility.targetArea: Field row 44px; chip dismiss 24px (WCAG 2.5.8 minimum), inherited from Tags and flagged rather than silently raised.
accessibility.$sc-note: 3.3.3 Error Suggestion genuinely applies (the refusals tell the user what to do), but it is NOT in the KNOWN_SC compliance lookup _build_integrity.py reads, and that lookup is a shared file this lane may not edit. Declared here rather than dropped silently — PROPOSED for the conductor: add 3.3.3 to the lookup.

antiPatterns: Dropping a duplicate or an over-limit value silently. A refusal the user cannot see is indistinguishable from a bug.
Discarding a half-typed value on blur. It is committed instead — the user typed it on purpose.
Drawing a second chip. This is the Tags chip; changes belong in Tags.
Claiming role=combobox without a list. There are no options here; announcing a collapsed listbox that never opens is worse than plain input semantics.
Signalling 'nearly at the limit' with colour or weight. The wording carries it — colour alone fails 1.4.1 and weight would need a raw font declaration TYPE-002 forbids.
